events.description: Went down under minimal contact, leading to Allan Nyom's controversial red card for Getafe; widely called out as a dive in the press.
Went down theatrically at Anfield in the Champions League; the dive was widely mocked and flooded social media with memes.
Won a second penalty against Sevilla with a theatrical dive; VAR declined to overturn it because there was contact after he had already gone down.
Won a contested penalty in the World Cup quarterfinal against Morocco; replays appeared to show he had gone down before contact from Mazraoui, and Moroccan players argued he had dived.
Named winner of the 2026 Barça Players' Association Award (Premi Barça Jugadors), recognizing the first-team player who showed the most fair play throughout the 2025–26 season.

Sent off in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final at Atlético Madrid after a VAR review overturned his initial yellow card; Julián Alvarez converted the resulting free kick as Barcelona lost 2-0.
Visibly directed frustration at the referee after missing the World Cup quarter-final penalty against Morocco, unhappy with the three-minute VAR delay before the kick.

Questioned a referee's neutrality after the 2-2 draw at Tottenham ("the people, they don't want us to win, but the referee has to be neutral"); admitted an FA charge and was fined £80,000 in March 2026.

Pushed his head into Erling Haaland's face during the 2-1 loss at Manchester City; escaped with a yellow on the field, but the Premier League's key match incidents panel later voted 3-2 that it was violent conduct deserving a red card.
